title: Why Only Christianity Satisfies BC4

canonical_node.axiom: Only a triune God (three persons, one essence) satisfies the boundary condition BC4 requiring exactly three observers for maximal coherence; all non-Trinitarian religions fail this condition.
definitions: BC4: Boundary condition requiring N_observers = 3 for C = C_max (zero-uncertainty self-referential system).
Trinity: Three distinct persons (Father, Son, Spirit) sharing one essence (homoousios).
N: Number of distinct personal observers.
C: Coherence measure; C_max is maximum coherence.
derivation: Self-knowledge requires a distinction between knower and known (T.1).
For a self-referential system to achieve zero uncertainty, exactly three observers are required (BC4).
Christianity posits three persons in one essence, satisfying N=3 and |E|=1.
Islam, Judaism, Unitarianism posit N=1; Buddhism N=0; Hinduism variants yield N=0,1, or 3 with |E|1.
canonical_node.action: Evaluate any proposed religion or worldview against BC4 by counting distinct personal observers and essences; if N=3 and |E|=1, it passes; otherwise, it fails.
boundary: Does not prove Christianity is true in all respects; only claims coherence with BC4.
Does not address other boundary conditions BC1-BC8 in full detail.
Does not claim to have examined all possible religions; logical space limited to N=0,1,2,3,many.
Does not assert that BC4 is the only necessary condition for truth.
test: For any religion R, compute N(R) and |E(R)|; check if N=3 and |E|=1.
Verify that the three persons are distinct yet share one essence (not tritheism or modalism).
Check that the religion affirms eternal self-knowledge and self-love without creation.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a formal criterion (N=3, |E|=1) to evaluate religious claims against BC4, enabling systematic comparison.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the prior axioms T.10 and D4 by operationalizing BC4 into a testable condition.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this node is removed, the uniqueness claim for Christianity loses its mathematical justification; BC4 remains but no religion is shown to satisfy it.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Quarantine as a conditional claim pending formal verification of BC4 derivation and uniqueness proof.

overstatement_risks: Equates BC4 with Trinity without independent justification.
Dismisses other religions based on simplified characterizations.
Assumes BC4 is necessary and sufficient for coherence.
kill_conditions: If BC4 is shown not to require N=3.
If another religion is shown to have N=3 and |E|=1.
If the derivation of BC4 from self-reference is invalid.
If the boundary conditions are shown to be arbitrary.
risk.lean_target: Formalize BC4 in a proof assistant (e.g., Lean) to verify the uniqueness claim.

plain_summary: This document argues that only Christianity, with its Trinity, satisfies a boundary condition BC4 requiring exactly three observers for a coherent self-referential God. It evaluates Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Unitarianism as failing. However, the proof is not formally established and relies on theological interpretations.
